theme: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

reports.title: Maureen Wharton
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

concerns.quote: No enquiry was made of Maureen as to the nature of her location and the potential support or assistance readily at hand or otherwise.
concerns.hazard: lack of inquiry into location and support

concerns.quote: No further enquiries were made to identify familial or social support which might or could have been enlisted or alerted to her presenting danger
concerns.hazard: failure to identify familial or social support

concerns.quote: No NEAS protocol appears to exist to assist personnel to initiate a response other than one limited to and directing an ambulance allocation
concerns.hazard: absence of protocol for non-ambulance response

concerns.quote: No working arrangement appears to exist to enlist the aid of other Agencies to support the patient or react more directly and in timely way to monitor and evaluate the nature of the presenting danger
a period of 3.45 hours elapsed between the first call and the arrival of an Ambulance crew at Maureen's side

reports.title: Richard Burgess
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: the Trust employs specialist Psychiatrists who are trained to work with patients with dementia, in addition to Care of the Elderly nurses, who provide training and support to staff. The Trust also employs Activity Coordinators who are all actively involved as part of the MDT process and has recently trained 10 members of staff to provide dementia care mapping training across the relevant wards.
promises.summary: Train staff in dementia care mapping and mapping training across wards

concerns.quote: the provision of a multidisciplinary team of professionals with suitable skills, qualifications and competencies commensurate with their role and the specialty of dementia care
concerns.hazard: lack of multidisciplinary team with appropriate skills and competencies

concerns.quote: a prevention model and approach for dementia care that proactively uses detailed assessment, intervention and evaluation of changing care, needs and risks of the individual in order to provide therapeutic interventions and reduce the need for medication
concerns.hazard: lack of proactive prevention model for dementia care

concerns.quote: the evidence of assessments or the application of assessments of the impact of a person's difficulties, including cognitive and neurological difficulties, polypharmacy, psychological and personality, mental and physical health, social, environmental and care practices, emotions, belief and thoughts of the person
concerns.hazard: insufficient assessment of individual's difficulties and risks

concerns.quote: a continuous engagement with the family in the
concerns.hazard: lack of continuous family engagement in triangle of care

concerns.quote: a focus on the person, asserting absolute value of the person, an individualised approach, while understanding the world from the person's perspective and provision of a social environment that supports psychological and physical needs
concerns.hazard: insufficient person-centred care and social environment

links.explanation: Both reports highlight insufficient involvement of family or social support in patient care. The earlier report notes a lack of enquiry to identify such support, while the later report stresses absent continuous engagement with the family.
links.earlier_quote: No further enquiries were made to identify familial or social support which might or could have been enlisted or alerted to her presenting danger
links.later_quote: - a continuous engagement with the family in the "triangle of care", including regular communication and updating life stories
